steps: Install the current plugin build in IntelliJ with the New UI dark theme and display scaling around 150%. The frame's search field is about 290 px wide against FILTER_WIDTH_PX = 200, which matches main-large.png's toolbar.

Open a .jsonl log of Rust tracing JSON lines, each with timestamp, level (TRACE/DEBUG/INFO), fields.message plus extra fields, and target values such as ai_agent_dashboard_lib::usage_limits, ::http_server, ::log_watcher and ::notifications. This is the same ai-agent-dashboard log family seen in main-large.png, so the JSONL split editor opens with its toolbar.
In the JSONL editor toolbar, leave the Level combo on "All".
Open the Target combo and pick ai_agent_dashboard_lib::usage_limits so the combo button shows that full target name.
Leave the Filter search field empty and unfocused.

Screenshot the toolbar row. Crop horizontally from just left of the "Level:" label to just past the right edge of the Filter search field, leaving out the pane selectors on the left and the "Total entries" stats on the right. Keep the full toolbar height (54 px, the same as the toolbar-panels.png and toolbar-stats.png crops).

screenshots.shows: Right-click popup over the Formatted pane, where "client=claude event=Stop" is selected on an "event -> set" line; the popup lists Filter by "client=claude event=Stop", a separator, and Copy Ctrl+C.

steps: Build and run the plugin in a sandbox IDE (runIde) that uses the same dark theme as the other screenshots in docs/screenshots.

Open a .jsonl log in Rust tracing JSON format. Each line is {timestamp, level, target, fields:{message, ...}}, from the AI agent dashboard (target ai_agent_dashboard_lib::...), the same log family as the committed fixtures in docs/screenshots/capture/fixtures/. The file needs hook-event lines whose message is "event -> set" with fields client=claude, event=Stop / UserPromptSubmit / Notification and chat_id=intellij-jsonl-extension. It also needs usage_limits lines whose message is "usage poll success" with fields five_hour_raw=37.0 seven_day_raw=82.0. In the visible stretch, one usage-poll line sits between runs of event -> set lines.
Show the Formatted pane (Left panel = Formatted). Clear any Level, Target or text filter so the mixed hook-event and usage-poll lines are visible.
In the Formatted pane, drag-select the text "client=claude event=Stop" on an "event -> set ... event=Stop" line, the fourth visible line in the crop.
Right-click the selection so the viewer popup opens next to it, showing Filter by "client=claude event=Stop", a separator, and Copy Ctrl+C. Do not hover any item, so no row is highlighted.

Crop to a strip about 868x222 px at the same display scale as the original (line pitch about 32 px). The strip covers seven formatted lines. The left crop edge cuts off the gutter, line numbers, timestamp, level and target, so each line starts at its message ("event -> set" / " usage poll success"). The right edge cuts through the popup's right border, and the bottom edge sits just below the popup.

Move the right cut inward off the slivers of the next glyphs it keeps: python ~/.claude/skills/docs-relevance/scripts/outline.py docs/screenshots/raw/context-menu-filter.png --sides none --clean right --reach 4 (one column, to 867 px)

steps: Run the plugin in a sandbox IDE (runIde) with a dark theme (the frame uses a dark New UI-style theme). Keep the default toolbar font and scaling so the strip comes out about 54 px tall.

Open a Rust tracing JSON .jsonl log, one object per line with timestamp, level, fields{message, five_hour_raw, seven_day_raw} and target, e.g. the ai_agent_dashboard usage_limits poller log, the family the committed fixtures in docs/screenshots/capture/fixtures/ come from. The visible subset must be 75 entries. The committed frame's session got there with Level: All and Target: aiagent_dashboard_lib::usage_limits, which toolbar-filter.png also shows.

Pick a file or moment where the earliest visible entry is about 10.5 hours old and the latest about 9 minutes old, so the labels read 'First entry: 10 hours 32 minutes ago' and 'Most recent: 9 minutes ago'.
Leave the timestamp labels in relative mode. If they show absolute dates, click 'First entry' once to toggle.
Make the editor wide enough that the toolbar shows all three stats labels without the overflow chevron. A narrower editor cuts the strip off after 'Total entries'.
Keep the pointer off the labels so no 'Click to switch between relative and absolute time' tooltip appears.

Capture the toolbar row and crop to the stats segment only: from just left of 'Total entries' to just right of 'Most recent: ... ago', full toolbar height (860x54 in the current file). Crop at the same scale and height as toolbar-panels.png and toolbar-filter.png so the three strips stay a matched series.
